course_name_original: Simulación Aplicada a Sistemas Eléctricos de Potencia
prerequisites: The students must certify that they have passed basic skills and competencies in power generation, transmission, and distribution systems. This can be either accomplished at his/her incoming student profile and CV or, if not covered there, by passing the related subjects of the first and second semesters. To those students who have not passed MCEESP02-C-002 it is not recommended to course this subject. It is nearly impossible to use simulation tools for Electrical Power Systems without adequate theoretical background.

learning_outcomes.text: Being original in the development and application of ideas within a research environment.
Giving solution to problems in a new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environment, regarding their branch of knowledge
Being capable of integrating knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments with ethic and social liability constraints.
Being able to communicate justified decisions and conclusions both to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Developing the skills for autonomous learning.
Acquiring knowledge about the main mathematic tools used in the analysis, modeling, and simulation of Electrical Power Systems.
Getting used to the use of software in the analysis, design, simulation, monitoring, control, and supervision of Electrical Power Systems.
Being able of doing a critical analysis of the information extracted from measurement instrumentations in Electrical Power Systems,
Assessment of the latent risks during the use of electrical energy, as well as those of industrial installations; understanding the necessity of safety elements and protection measurements.
Practical and experimental verification of monitoring and controlling of Electrical Energy Conversion Systems, including their safe operation.
Development of skills regarding teamwork, different roles within a workgroup, and different ways of organization in research teams.
Development of the ability to analyze and synthesize specialized technical information.
Development of the ability to assimilate and communicate technical information in English.
Development of the ability for planning and organizing technical studies.
Development of the ability to communicate justified decisions and conclusions both to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Understanding of the importance and the area of application of electrical power systems for the generation, transmission, and distribution of electrical energy.
Characterization and modeling of the main energy sources and electric power loads.
Development of the ability to understand the basics of the dynamic modeling of electrical power systems.
Identification of the main characteristics, design strategies, and constructive elements of the Electrical Power Systems.
Ability to analyze the different strategies for grid connection, from both technical and economic points of view.
To know the design processes and technologies involved in the design of an electrical power system
Management of different environments for simulation modeling and analysis of an entire power system, taking into account the multidisciplinary nature of the knowledge that it involves.
Understanding the problem of the transient phenomena in power systems, and application of different techniques for their removal.

syllabus_topics: SIMULATION AND ANALYSIS OF ELECTRICAL POWER SYSTEMS WITH MATLAB/SIMULINK
Review of Sympower Systems from Mathworks
Development of models for the analysis of Electrical Power Systems (Power Flow and Faults)
SIMULATION OF POWER SYSTEMS WITH DIGISILENT POWER FACTORY (PF)
Introduction to the use of Digisilent (brief course presented during the lectures and available in the virtual campus under different formats)
Practical study, based on cases provided by the software, of all type of analyses on different types of Electrical Power Systems.
assessment_rules: The final mark is composed of 50% from a final project, 30% from practical exercises, and 20% from a written examination. A minimum score of 50% must be obtained in the practical exercises (1.5 points summing the three practices) and a minimum of 30% of correct answers in the written test. To pass the course, a total of 5 points (50% global) must be obtained. For the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of 40% written examination (more developed answers), 40% practical examination (two problems with Mathworks Simulink and Digisilent PF), and 20% practical exercises with a short report. A minimum of 30% of the positive score in each of these components must be obtained.
bibliography: The whole documentation will be available online. Materials used during the lectures will be uploaded to the Virtual Campus of the University of Oviedo. Particularly, two short courses of Digilent PF and Mathworks Simulink will be included. Different digital formats will be used: Powerpoint presentations used during the lectures and YT online videos. The aim of the latter is to allow the students to review the lectures whenever they need them.
